name: @stonedogcode/howto
description: A how-to documentation surface for applications: markdown articles that describe themselves in frontmatter, section manifests, per-article tables of contents, search, and access control supplied by the host.
author: StoneDogCode L.L.C.
//workspaces: `demo` only, and it is private. The `files` list below ships src/ alone, so the demo travels with the repository and never with the tarball.
//exports: This package ships TypeScript SOURCE, not a bundled dist/, for the same reason @stonedogcode/style does: the React layer is styled with Panda CSS, which extracts styles by statically parsing source at the CONSUMER's build. A pre-bundled dist would emit class names the consumer's Panda never generated a stylesheet for. Consumers transpile us (Next.js: `transpilePackages: ['@stonedogcode/howto']`) and add our src to their panda `include` globs.
//files: The __tests__ exclusion is load-bearing, not tidiness. Consumers add `node_modules/@stonedogcode/howto/src/**` to their Panda `include` globs, so anything shipped under src/ is statically parsed at THEIR build — and the tests import jest globals and render fixture markup. They also ship a test suite nobody can run to every consumer.

scripts.//dev: The demo. Its own workspace, so one `npm install` at the root is enough and react resolves to a single hoisted copy — two Reacts in one tree fail at runtime with 'Invalid hook call', pointing at a component rather than at the install that caused it.
scripts.//test: Jest runs as ESM (see jest.config.cjs), which needs the VM modules flag.
scripts.//gate: The demo is type-checked here too. It is not published, but it is the worked example consumers copy from, and an example that does not compile is worse than none.
scripts.gate: npm run type-check && npm run type-check:demo && npm run lint && npm run test

//peerDependencies: react/react-dom are peers ONLY. Listing them as dependencies too makes npm install a second copy into this package, and two Reacts in one tree fail at runtime with 'Invalid hook call' — a failure that points at the consumer's component, not at this manifest.
//publish:stonedog-howto: Run from a terminal, interactively — npm prompts for the 2FA one-time password and the login flow needs a browser. It refuses a checkout that is detached, dirty, or behind origin/main, refuses a tarball containing tests or missing an entry point, and proves the result by installing from the registry into a temp directory.
//publishConfig: A scoped package defaults to RESTRICTED on npm, which requires a paid plan and would fail the publish. Declaring it here means the intent travels with the manifest instead of depending on someone remembering --access public.
